Learn biology and chemistry from the beginning

Learn chemical formulas, dilution, proteins and inheritance through drawings and worked examples. Start with water and follow the interactive science lessons.

How do you read a chemical formula?

H stands for hydrogen and O for oxygen. In H₂O the small 2 applies to hydrogen. Draw H–O–H and count the three atoms in one water molecule.

What changes when you add water to a solution?

You have 0.01 mol of solute in 100 mL of solution. Concentration is the amount in moles divided by volume in litres. That gives 0.01 / 0.10 = 0.10 mol/L.

Add water to reach 200 mL. The same amount of solute now occupies twice the volume, so its concentration falls to 0.05 mol/L.

Why can 35 cysteines form at most 17 bridges?

A residue is the part of an amino acid incorporated into a protein chain. Cysteine has a sulfur atom in its side chain. One S–S bridge joins the sulfur atoms of two residues. Hence 35 = 2 × 17 + 1.

Compare 34 and 35 in the model. Both give a maximum of 17. Bridges help maintain the protein’s shape. Pockets in albumin can bind the hydrophobic parts of fatty acids, helping carry them through plasma.

How do you calculate a chance across two children?

In an Aa × aa cross, the first parent is equally likely to pass on A or a. The second always passes on a. Each child therefore has a ½ chance of Aa and a ½ chance of aa.

For two independent births the chance of two aa children is ½ × ½ = ¼. Every other outcome includes at least one Aa child. Together those outcomes have probability 1 − ¼ = ¾.
